---
title: "Reading copies"
---

Rill never shows you a live web page. It shows a stored reading copy: a
cleaned Markdown version of the article, saved with where it came from, when,
and how it was made. Copies don't change once saved. A newer copy is added
alongside the old one, and Ask Rill and Orientation always know which copy
they read.

A story can have three kinds of copy, and the reader labels each one:

- A feed copy is made from the content in the feed itself. Rill makes one the
  first time you open a story, so the story appears straight away. It keeps
  paragraphs, images, links, and lists, but many feeds only include an
  excerpt.
- An extracted copy is the full article, taken from the public page with
  [Defuddle](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle). Extraction can leave out or
  reorder parts of a page.
- A captured copy is sent from your own browser. Use it for pages Rill can't
  fetch itself, such as articles behind a login.

## Preparing full articles

Rill prepares full articles in a separate background process, so reading
never waits on it:

- after each feed refresh, for public articles from the past seven days that
  don't have a copy yet;
- after each scheduled `poll_feeds()` run, for up to 100 articles or ten
  minutes of work;
- when you choose **Prepare full article** on a story, or **Prepare** in the
  Today view.

When a full copy is ready for the story you're reading, Rill offers
**Load full article** rather than swapping the text under you. Copies you
captured in your browser are never replaced.

Failed attempts are retried after 5, 10, 20, 40, and then 80 minutes. After
five failures Rill stops retrying on its own, but you can still retry from the
story once the last wait has passed. Some publishers block extraction. Those stories stay readable
from the feed copy, and **Original** opens the publisher's page.

Only public article URLs from your subscriptions are sent for extraction,
never captured pages or anything about your reading. Rill keeps YouTube and
Vimeo embeds, using their privacy-enhanced players in a sandbox, and removes
other embedded frames and scripts.

## Choosing an extractor

By default Rill sends article URLs to the hosted Defuddle API at
`defuddle.md`, which fetches and extracts the page. Set `DEFUDDLE_API_KEY` if
you have a key.

To keep extraction inside your installation, use the copy of the Defuddle
command-line tool that ships with Rill. It needs Node.js 18 or later, or
Deno 2 or later (Posit Connect Cloud provides Deno), and downloads nothing at
run time:

```text
DEFUDDLE_BACKEND=local
DEFUDDLE_COMMAND=bundled
```

To use your own installation instead, run `npm install -g defuddle` and set
`DEFUDDLE_COMMAND=defuddle`, or set `DEFUDDLE_COMMAND` to the path of the
executable. Rill runs `defuddle parse <url> --md --frontmatter` and applies
the same public-URL check as the hosted backend.

## Capturing pages from your browser

When `RILL_CAPTURE_TOKEN` is set, the app accepts captured pages at
`POST /api/v1/captures`. A browser extension or bookmarklet extracts the page
in your signed-in browser and sends Rill the Markdown. Rill never sees your
browser's cookies or passwords.

```json
{
  "capture_id": "3f87de90-4302-4f3e-9e84-2f5d4c966abd",
  "source_url": "https://example.com/article",
  "canonical_url": "https://example.com/article",
  "title": "An article worth keeping",
  "author": "Ada Lovelace",
  "site": "Example",
  "published_at": "2026-08-29T12:30:00Z",
  "markdown": "# An article worth keeping\n\nExact captured text.",
  "captured_at": "2026-08-30T22:15:00Z",
  "producer": "my-rill-clipper",
  "producer_version": "1.0.0",
  "metadata": {
    "extraction_mode": "article"
  }
}
```

```sh
curl --request POST "https://your-rill.example/api/v1/captures" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $RILL_CAPTURE_TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @capture.json
```

`capture_id`, `source_url`, `title`, `markdown`, `captured_at`, and `producer`
are required. `source_url` must be a public HTTP or HTTPS address, and the
request body can be at most 5 MiB.

Rill responds with `201` and the new entry and document IDs. Sending the same
capture again returns `200` with the original IDs, so retries are safe.
Reusing a `capture_id` with different content returns `409`.

If the URL matches a story already in your Library, the capture becomes that
story's reading copy. Otherwise Rill adds an unread story under
**Local captures**. Captures belong to the Reader who owns the token: nobody
else sees them, and they never replace another Reader's copy. Rill stores
only a hash of the token.

## Preparing copies from R

`prepare_today()` prepares copies for everything published today, in the time
zone of the R process. It needs `DATABASE_URL` and uses the same settings as
the app. Each failure comes with a reference that matches an entry in the
server log:

```r
result <- rill::prepare_today()
result$failures
```
